title: Cache Governor: Prefetch Sculptor and Safe Apply
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Implement a 'Cache Governor' service that generates per-prefix prefetch budgets and TTL adjustments informed by hit-rate forecasts and batching characteristics, and provides a throttled, observable safe-apply path for changes. This ticket scopes the model, an offline simulator, and a shadow-canary rollout plan.

Why: Current static TTLs and coarse prefix rules either waste memory (over-prefetch) or increase per-request cost (cold prefixes). We can reduce token-level cost while protecting latency SLOs by combining forecasting, batching-awareness, and conservative apply controls.

Approach:
1) Hit-rate forecasting: build a lightweight exponential-smoothing + Bayesian shrinkage model per-prefix that predicts short-horizon hit uplift from prefetch windows. Inputs: prefix QPS, prefix entropy estimate, recent hit volatility, observed batch sizes.
2) Prefetch sculptor: translate forecast uplift to a small prefetch budget (items and TTL delta) that is batching-aware (avoids prefetching beyond typical batch window to minimize KV contention).
3) Safe apply engine: staged application process with shadow trials, canary percentages tied to cost and latency gates, automated rollback triggers, and a manual-override path.
4) Integrations: metrics export to Grafana, PRD+spec link, and a small runtime hook so Dedicated/Private can opt into the governor.

Deliverables: spec doc, simulator notebook, scoring service (read-only) + controller (apply path), Grafana dashboard, one E2E canary run and post-mortem.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A simulator that reproduces observed hit-rate uplift within 10% absolute on historical traces; 2) Prefetch budgets generated per-prefix with deterministic inputs; 3) Safe-apply path implements shadow trials and canary ramp with rollback triggers; 4) End-to-end test showing >=5% average token-cost reduction on targeted workload without >5% regressions in p99 latency; 5) Monitoring dashboards and runbook updated; 6) Security review completed if requested.
comments: 2026-02-18 - Aisha: Initial write-up and scope. Created simulator skeleton and exported sample traces from production shadow cluster.
2026-02-25 - Marcus: Reviewed forecasting approach; recommended adding batch-size conditioning to avoid prefetches that span multiple micro-batches.
2026-03-02 - Eng lead (Elena Park): Approved prototype plan; suggested a conservative canary (1% -> 5% -> 20% over 72h) with automatic rollback on cost delta >8% or p99 latency increase >3%.

2026-03-05 - Data Sci (Omar Ruiz): Ran first simulator sweep (7 days) against two workloads: low-entropy chat and high-entropy search. Results: median hit uplift 12% (chat), 4% (search); cache churn increased <2% in both cases.
2026-03-08 - Marcus: Opened PR for scoring service (https://github.com/redwood-inference/prefetch-governor/pull/1382). Requesting review from infra and runtime teams for integration hooks.
2026-03-09 - QA: Added test plan to validate safe-apply rollback when the shadow trial shows increased eviction rate or customer-facing errors.
2026-03-10 - Marcus: Running a staged internal canary on staging with 0.5% traffic. Early telemetry looks green; continuing to 1% tomorrow.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Shadow-only scoring for 2 weeks (no apply). Phase 1: Internal canary 0.5% traffic, monitor 48h. Phase 2: Gradual ramp 0.5->1->5->20% over 7 days with automated checks. Phase 3: Targeted cohort expansion to high-benefit prefixes. Rollback triggers: cost delta >8% sustained for 1h, p99 latency increase >3% sustained 30m, eviction-rate change >10% vs baseline. Manual abort allowed at any stage.
experiment_results_summary: Simulator run notes (2026-03-02): used 14 days of traffic for two customer workloads. Prefetch sculptor with conservative budget (max 3 items/prefix, TTL +30s) produced a 6.8% token-cost reduction on weighted mix; hit-rate uplift concentrated in top 5% prefixes. Observed trade-off: small increase in KV writes (~1.7%) and negligible p99 latency change. Next experiment will tune per-prefix budget caps and include eviction-aware penalty in cost function.
